newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan July foreign currency deposits hit record.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan July foreign currency deposits hit record.

text.p: Taiwan's foreign currency deposits outstanding hit a record-high of T$277.12 billion in July after recent rate cuts by the central bank, the central bank said on Tuesday in a statement.
Following recent interest rate cuts, investors prefer to hold foreign currency deposits rather than Taiwan dollars, a central bank official told journalists.

He also said that exporters, in order to avoid risks in exchanging foreign currency, had been gradually getting used to paying for their imported raw materials directly by foreign currency, instead of using Taiwan dollars as they had previously.
"This made them hold more foreign currency on hand that they earned from exports," the official said.
In July, the bank said in a statement that the main reasons for the increase of foreign currency deposits outstanding were Taiwan's continuous trade surplus and persistent inflows of foreign funds.
The July figure was up from June's T$272.77 billion, it said.

The July figures were in sharp contrast to the same month a year earlier, when foreign currency deposits were T$130.12 billion. Officials said frictions between Taiwan and China had fuelled the rise in foreign currency deposits.

China, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province, conducted a series of wargames near the island in March to warn the Taiwan electorate not to vote for independence in elections, further triggering surges in foreign currency deposits.

Investors have also transferred their money to foreign currency holdings, with the money remaining in Taiwan. The actual capital outflow was not as serious as expected, central bank officials have said.

Taiwan's July time deposits and time savings deposits also hit record highs of T$2.304 trillion and T$5.14 trillion respectively, due to a poor stock market performance and investor anticipation of rate cuts, the central bank official said.
